name: How do luxury builders handle long-lead items like windows and stone?

mainEntity.name: What happens if custom windows, cabinetry, or imported stone are delayed during a luxury build?
mainEntity.text: What happens if custom windows, cabinetry, or imported stone are delayed during a luxury build?

acceptedAnswer.text: Long-lead items are one of the biggest schedule risks in luxury custom home building. Custom windows, specialty doors, cabinetry, stone slabs, appliances, and smart-home components may take months to arrive, and some require shop drawings or manufacturer approvals before ordering. If these items are selected late, the schedule can slip even when labor is ready. A good builder should flag long-lead items during preconstruction, tie them to a procurement calendar, and track approvals closely. Homeowners should ask which items must be selected before permits are issued, which can wait until construction, and how substitutions are approved if the original product is delayed or unavailable. This is especially important in Los Angeles, where project timelines are often already stretched by permitting and site constraints.
acceptedAnswer.description: Long-lead items can delay the entire project if they are not ordered early enough. Luxury builders should identify these items during preconstruction, lock selections early, and coordinate delivery dates with the construction schedule.
